  • Proven track record of shipping successful, production-ready mobile applications within the fintech or blockchain/onchain sectors.
  • Strong product intuition, keen attention to UX details, and a high degree of reliability.
  • Excellent communication skills with the ability to collab

title: Software Engineer, Front End & Design
description:
About CircuitHub

CircuitHub is reshaping electronics manufacturing with The Grid, a factory-scale robotics platform that makes small-batch, high-mix electronics assembly radically more efficient. Think semiconductor-fab precision applied to the chaotic world of prototyping and low-volume production: a 10x throughput improvement in one of the world's most foundational industries.

We've raised $45M from top-tier investors including Plural, Y Combinator and Google Ventures, and we're already profitable. Our customers include a major EV maker, a top AI lab and many of the worlds largest companies.

The Grid isn't a prototype. It's live, scaling fast and delivering real revenue, and we're building the team that will scale it further.

What you'll do

  • Shape the customer experience. Upload, quoting, ordering and our board viewer on circuithub.com.

  • Make internal tools a pleasure. Our admin dashboard runs purchasing, planning, recruiting and the AI agents that do more and more of the work. Make dense, data-heavy screens clear and fast.

  • Design for the factory floor. Screens operators read at a glance while robots move around them.

  • Own the design system. Bring our brand, components and patterns together across web apps and machine screens.

  • Design for agents. Work out how people should review, steer and trust the work of AI agents.

What we look for

  • You've shipped full-featured web apps in TypeScript and React, and you can show us.

  • A real eye for design, both UI and UX. A portfolio we can look at matters more than a job title.

  • You enjoy owning a product end to end, from talking to users to deploying.

  • You use coding agents to move faster and take full ownership of what they produce.

  • Bonus: data visualisation, Elm or other functional languages, industrial or operator interfaces.

Stack

  • Web: TypeScript, React, TanStack (Start, Router, Query, Table), Tailwind, Radix, Bun

title: Software Engineer, Haskell
description:
About CircuitHub

CircuitHub is reshaping electronics manufacturing with The Grid, a factory-scale robotics platform that makes small-batch, high-mix electronics assembly radically more efficient. Think semiconductor-fab precision applied to the chaotic world of prototyping and low-volume production: a 10x throughput improvement in one of the world's most foundational industries.

We've raised $45M from top-tier investors including Plural, Y Combinator and Google Ventures, and we're already profitable. Our customers include a major EV maker, a top AI lab and many of the worlds largest companies.

The Grid isn't a prototype. It's live, scaling fast and delivering real revenue, and we're building the team that will scale it further.

Overview

  • CircuitHub is primarily built using a combination of Haskell, Nix, and PostgreSQL, deployed to both AWS and bare metal machines. We use a significant amount of open-source technology, and also try and give back where possible (for example, both Rel8 and Fast Downward Haskell bindings).

  • CircuitHub spans a vast problem space. Challenges include computer vision (OpenCV), machine learning (PyTorch), hard optimization problems (Z3/MiniZinc/OR-Tools), and all the normal engineering challenges of building both web-based customer-facing and internal tooling.

  • We work on manufacturing execution systems, enterprise resource planning, and robotics. An old video from Haskell Exchange 2019 hints at what we are up to on the robotics side. We have progressed significantly since then!

  • These roles are remote (any location), in-person, or hybrid, depending on preference.

  • We have offices in South Deerfield - USA, Cambridge, and London, UK.

  • Salary depends on the candidate and location, but as guidance in the UK, a likely range is £80k to £125k and in the US $125k to $250k, with additional equity.

  • CircuitHub has raised $45M from top-tier VCs and has been going for about ten years. CircuitHub is profitable, with tens of millions in revenue. Small team (CircuitHub is ~50 employees) with tremendous growth opportunity and low risk. We are aiming to 10x capacity through 2027 in both our existing Massachusetts factory and expand into Europe.

description:
At Kpler, we are dedicated to helping our clients navigate complex markets with ease. By simplifying global trade information and providing valuable insights, we empower organisations to make informed decisions in commodities, energy, and maritime sectors.
 
Since our founding in 2014, we have focused on delivering top-tier intelligence through user-friendly platforms. Our team of over 850 experts from 69 countries works tirelessly to transform intricate data into actionable strategies, ensuring our clients stay ahead in a dynamic market landscape. Join us to leverage cutting-edge innovation for impactful results and experience unparalleled support on your journey to success.
 

About the Role

As a Software Engineer on the founding Connected Supply Chain team, you will build and run the core services extending Kpler’s real-time trade intelligence platform beyond marine coverage into North American inland supply chains. Operating on a high-autonomy "you build it, you run it" model, you will carry sensor telemetry from field hardware to paying customers through streaming ingestion pipelines, robust APIs, and user-facing features. By uniting crude pipeline remote sensors, rail, and waterway data with existing maritime tracking, your work will directly deliver a single connected view from production basin to export terminal.

  • Build and maintain scalable ingestion and processing pipelines for sensor, rail, and waterway data using Python, Kafka, and Airflow.

As Engineering Manager at Cosuno, you will lead a team of full stack engineers while staying deeply hands-on: you'll spend 60–80% of your time coding, reviewing, and shaping the architecture alongside your team. title: Frontend Engineer - Agentic AI
description:
About Us 

Hawk is the leading provider of AI-supported anti-money laundering and fraud detection technology. Banks and payment providers globally are using Hawk’s powerful combination of traditional rules and explainable AI to improve the effectiveness of their AML compliance and fraud prevention by identifying more crime while maximizing efficiency by reducing false positives. With our solution, we are playing a vital role in the global fight against Money Laundering, Fraud, or the financing of terrorism. We offer a culture of mutual trust, support and passion – while providing individuals with opportunities to grow professionally and make a difference in the world. 

Your Mission

As a Frontend Engineer at Hawk, you will build and maintain the user interface of our agentic AI Investigation Agent. This is the product where compliance analysts configure AI workflows, watch autonomous investigations run, and review, question and act on what the agent concludes.

The frontend is a modern TypeScript monorepo made of a host application and a growing set of independently deployable microfrontends. These remotes are designed to be built once and used in two places: our new shadcn/ui-based Investigation Agent and our existing Material UI-based Case Manager. Your job is to understand this codebase deeply, keep it healthy, and ship new features with care, from the component level all the way to how it is built and deployed.

What You'll Work On:

  • Features: Build product features end to end in React and TypeScript, such as workflow graph editors, investigation timelines, data-heavy tables and dashboards that make agentic AI output understandable for analysts.

  • Microfrontends: Develop and maintain Module Federation remotes, keep remote/host contracts stable, and make sure features fit into both the Investigation Agent and the MUI-based Case Manager.

  • Design system and data layer: Contribute to our shared shadcn/ui + Tailwind component library (documented in Storybook), and consume our Python/FastAPI backends through OpenAPI-generated clients with TanStack Query and Router.

  • Build, test and deploy: Work in a pnpm + Turborepo monorepo with GitHub Actions CI, Vitest and Playwright tests, and deployments to AWS including per-PR preview environments.

  • Collaboration

title: Software Engineer, AI Coding Tasks
description:
We're looking for experienced software engineers to build AI coding tasks from a codebase they know well. US$1,000 per task, and you can do as many tasks as you want.

 

You turn a real change from a repository you know into a task that today's best AI coding models struggle with: hard for the models, but fair for a skilled engineer. Your tasks are used to measure and train AI coding models.

 

Remote, any location. US$1,000 per task that passes review. Minimum of one task a week, about 10 hours a week.

 

How it works

 

  1. Apply. Complete a short screener interview and upload your resume.
  2. Propose. Once you're selected, pick a change from a repository you know and submit a short proposal. We approve it or suggest a better candidate.
  3. Build. In our platform, set up the repository as it was before the change, then write the brief, the correct solution and the grading checks.
  4. Stress-test. Try lazy, incorrect and shortcut solutions and make sure your checks catch them.
  5. Model testing. Run your task against leading AI models until strong models often fail but a skilled engineer can clearly solve it.
  6. Review. A reviewer checks your task and you revise it. Most tasks take more than one round.
  7. Next task. Once your task is accepted, start another.

  • 2+ years of professional software engineering

  • You can explain a change clearly and concisely, in your own words

Nice to have

 

  • Deep expertise in one area, such as databases, compilers, distributed systems, security or infrastructure
  • Experience building agent tasks or RL environments

 

Terms

 

  • US$1,000 for each task that passes our quality review, paid directly to you
  • Once your proposal is qualified, you sign Askable's contract and accept its terms

logistics. It is an operational problem before it is an environmental one, and
in our hands it is mostly an engineering one.

We are hiring a senior engineer who works across our web frontend and our
infrastructure — the same two codebases, in the same week. Someone who ships a
product screen on Monday, changes an identity-provider flow on Wednesday, and
considers those the same job.

We are looking for a broad profile rather than a specialist. The next year is
mostly platform work with a user-facing edge — user management, API gateway
management, payments, SEO, and a great deal of compliance, GDPR and ISO 27001.

If you are passionate about the environment, proactive and pragmatic in getting
things done, and love to work in a complex but fascinating industry where you
learn every day — then this is the place for you.

The work in front of us

Some of the items on our tech roadmap for the coming year. Bets are picked a
cycle at a time and shared out, so you would take the ones that suit you and
grow into the rest.

  • Product and marketing UI in React — multi-brand, WCAG AA, strong on
    technical SEO, fast enough to hold a performance budget.
  • User management and identity — Keycloak realms, organisation hierarchies,
    partner brokering, and the entitlement model in the app.
  • API gateway work in APISIX — routes, plugins and auth policy as code.
  • Payments and billing.
  • ISO 27001 and GDPR — access control, change management, audit logging,

used to working things out — with a team and with agents, rather than alone.

Radix; Jest and Playwright; GitHub Actions; HAProxy. Most of what we write is
TypeScript, strict — though our core API is Java and Spring, and the identity

The HOLOPLOT Matrix Array is a new type of sound system built around precise, software-defined control of sound in three dimensions - grounded in physics and implemented through a combination of custom hardware and purpose-built software. Our infrastructure is defined as code and evolves through the same review and release process as the rest of our software. title: Staff/Senior Software Engineer - Hydris - Golang (d/f/m)
description:
New Challenge

About Us 
Project Q GmbH ("Q") is a Germany-based DefenseTech company with offices in Berlin and Munich. We network market-available sensors, effectors, or situational awareness systems into a tactical IoT backbone that reliably provides armed forces and security agencies with cross-domain information superiority — automated, scalable, and cost-efficient.

Our solutions integrate seamlessly into existing defense and maritime infrastructures, delivering fast data fusion and AI-enhanced analytics for robust situational awareness in dynamic environments. We build platform-agnostic systems that enable real interoperability across domains.

As a Staff Software Engineer, you'll directly impact the technical direction of our orchestration products – Hydris – the coordination engine for sensors and mission systems, and the interoperability API that underpins it. 

You'll work at the layer where heterogeneous real-world systems like radars, AIS receivers, LoRa mesh radios, satellite feeds, and C2 platforms become a single coherent picture. The problems lie in distributed systems, protocols, and data modeling areas. They play out in environments that are bandwidth-constrained, intermittently connected, and operationally unforgiving. 

The role is deeply hands-on, but it expects you to shape what we build and how we build it, not just deliver what's specified.

What you'll do
Core engine development

  • Design and build the systems that power Hydris.
  • Go is your primary language. You should be comfortable reading Rust and TypeScript across the codebase, even if you're not writing in them day-to-day.
  • Own the architecture of a system that must run reliably on edge hardware, in disconnected mesh networks, and at scale — often all of that simultaneously.
Protocol and integration architecture
  • Evolve the schema that defines how every sensor, asset, and mission system talks to Hydris.
  • Make API design decisions that hold up across our client libraries without creating a maintenance burden.
  • Continue refining the integration framework that lets Hydris connect to new sensor types, data sources, and command systems.
  • Set the patterns for how built-in integrations (ADS-B, AIS, ASTERIX, Meshtastic, SpaceTrack, TAK, federation) are structured, tested, and maintained.
  • Make it straightforward for external developers and system vendors to build their own plugins/integrations to Hydris.
Distributed systems
  • Architect the peer-to-peer mesh and federation layer that keeps Hydris operational in disconnected, denied, intermittent, and limited-bandwidth environments.
  • Solve the hard coordination problems: conflict resolution across federated nodes, eventual consistency of entity state, and track correlation across unreliable links.
  • Ensure the system degrades gracefully rather than failing completely

AISLE is building the AI that finds, fixes, and verifies software vulnerabilities autonomously - an end-to-end system that closes the gap between when a vulnerability appears and when it's safely patched. title: Founding Engineer (Remote - EEA/UK)
description:
Founding Engineer


Role can be based remotely in the EEA or hybrid in our London or Munich offices.

Fixed software is the wrong shape for logistics, because every team runs its processes differently. Tare is our solution. Combining agentic AI with deterministic logic means Tare fits to any customer but runs the same way every single time. We have just closed our pre-seed funding round with a top European VC and we are now looking for a founding engineer to build Tare with us.

About Tarebase

We're Dom and Felix, the two co-founders of Tarebase. Dom is a former SVP at a global unicorn, overseeing tens of millions in global carrier spend, with deep logistics domain experience from Amazon, Nestle and EY. Felix was a founding engineer at Raycast and has spent more than two decades building software systems. We've raised pre-seed funding from a top-tier European VC and are building our MVP together with early design partners, who will become our first customers. As our first employee, you'd have a real say in both the product and the engineering decisions behind it.

Logistics is difficult to run well, and experienced people are hard to hire. Smaller businesses often pay too much for shipping, struggle to give customers a good delivery experience, and can't match larger competitors' technology or hiring budgets. The software available to them is often expensive, dated or too cumbersome. We want to make logistics less of a burden so these businesses can spend more time selling their products.They're the customers we want to build for: Europe alone has around 26 million SMEs, employing more than 100 million people.

Just putting a chat interface and GPT-wrapper on top of the problem is not what we're building. We're combining extraction and analysis, workflow automation, agentic and compiled AI with deterministic, verifiable logic. Recent advances in AI make more of this possible, but building a system that does it reliably is still hard. We're looking for someone who wants to advance the state of the art in this area with us.

About you

The description below is an ideal, not a checklist. If you don't tick every box but feel ready for the challenges of being the first engineer at an early-stage startup, we'd still like to hear from you. What matters most to us is that you're motivated, committed, willing to stick with hard problems, and someone we can count on.

You have a strong technical background and a track record of building and shipping software systems, whether that's cloud backends, web applications, AI-supported systems or a mix of these. You enjoy working across engineering and product. You think like a product engineer: you care about UX/UI, and you want direct contact with customers and the people who use what you build.

We run it all on our own metal, our own network, our own datacenters — which means when something breaks, the fix is ours to write.

European Compute Units let enterprises commit to multi-year capacity on that infrastructure, and we are scaling toward a gigawatt of compute across Europe by 2030. You will design and ship the layer every sovereign AI deployment depends on.

THE ROLE

You will build our serverless containers product: the way developers run AI apps, MCP servers, APIs, and managed workers on our cloud without thinking about servers. Push a container, get an endpoint, scale from zero to thousands of instances and back down — across CPU and GPU.

On a hyperscaler, the serverless layer is a product someone else built. Here you build it end to end: the scheduler that decides where a container lands, the routing path a request takes, the machinery that turns a scaled-to-zero service into a warm instance before a customer notices. All of it runs on metal, network, and datacenters we own.

That tension is the product: scale-to-zero economics with cold starts in milliseconds, autoscaling that absorbs a launch spike without a config change, GPUs scheduled onto containers the way other platforms schedule CPU. The customers betting on this layer are the developers building the next generation of AI software on European infrastructure.

WHAT YOU WILL DO

- Build the container platform end to end: image delivery, placement, request routing, scale-up, scale-to-zero

description:

Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited.

THE TEAM

Mistral is building a sovereign AI cloud for Europe. Our customers in finance, healthcare, and the public sector run frontier models on European-jurisdiction infrastructure, and the Cloud Platform team builds the systems that make that possible — compute orchestration, Kubernetes, bare metal, storage, networking, and the datacenter fleet that runs it all.

We run it all on our own metal, our own network, our own datacenters — which means when something breaks, the fix is ours to write.

European Compute Units let enterprises commit to multi-year capacity on that infrastructure, and we are scaling toward a gigawatt of compute across Europe by 2030. You will design and ship the layer every sovereign AI deployment depends on.

THE ROLE

You will build storage on our cloud.

Block, filesystem, and object storage for training runs, sandboxed workloads, and general compute: you help decide what we build, what we buy, and how it adds up to storage our customers can bet a business on. Some layers we deploy and harden from best-in-class vendors. The ones that matter most we write ourselves in Go — S3-compatible object storage, tiering, backup and recovery, caching layers that put cold data on cheap spinning disks.

Storage is a strategic bet for this org: the systems you build will define how a gigawatt of European compute stores its data.

WHAT YOU WILL DO

- Build the storage stack — block, file, object — for training, sandbox, and general compute workloads.

- Design and write our own services in Go: S3-compatible APIs, tiering, backup and recovery, caching layers.

- Own the data plane: allocation, duplication, tiering, backup and recovery.

- Plan capacity across datacenters and across failure domains — petabytes, not terabytes.

At Wolt, we create technology that brings joy, simplicity and earnings to the neighborhoods of the world. In 2014 we started with delivery of restaurant food. Now we're building the delivery of (almost) everything and you'll find us in over 500 cities in 30 countries around the world. Working at Wolt isn't always easy, but it's definitely exciting. Here you'll learn more, build more, and ship more than in most other companies. We're building a new Feature Engineering Platform that will be the front door to ML development at global scale. As a Software Engineer on this team, you'll help build a seamless experience for ML practitioners across the company — from experimentation and exploration to deployment and monitoring.

Our mission is to make machine learning accessible and intuitive without compromising on power or performance. You'll work on a layered platform that supports both high-level declarative workflows and lower-level imperative APIs, all integrated into the environments our users already work in (like notebooks and internal sandboxes).

  • Curious and collaborative mindset — eager to learn from others and contribute broadly.
  • Experience with ML tooling, or data pipelines is a plus.

Unsere Mission: Connect every employee to everything they need in one touch.

 

Stellenausschreibung

KI-Orchestrierung steht im Zentrum der Zukunft von Flip. Flip Fusion, ein Multi-Agenten-System zur Code-Generierung, bildet das Herzstück unseres neuesten Produkts. Auch das Ask AI Agent Gateway und die Automatisierung durch Flip Flows laufen auf Fähigkeiten, die unsere KI-Engineers entwickeln und pflegen.

Als Lead AI Engineer übernimmst du die KI-Disziplin: Du verantwortest das Wie, also Architektur, Standards und technische Ausrichtung, über alle drei Bereiche hinweg, führst und entwickelst ein Team von drei AI-Engineers weiter und bleibst dabei hands-on an den anspruchsvollsten Problemen.

Was dich erwartet

  • KI-Architektur verantworten: Definiere eine kohärente KI-Architektur und einheitliche Standards für Flip Fusion, das Ask AI Agent Gateway und Flip Flows, und stimme sie aufeinander ab.

  • Die größte Herausforderung annehmen: Multi-Agenten-Systeme, die für konkrete Anwendungsfälle gebaut sind, aber generisch genug bleiben, um unterschiedliche Kund:innen zu bedienen, immer im Spannungsfeld zwischen hohen Ansprüchen, Machbarkeit, Zuverlässigkeit und Kosteneffizienz.

  • Die Disziplin führen und weiterentwickeln: Übernimm die disziplinarische Führung für drei KI-Engineers und hilf ihnen dabei, sich zu Engineers zu entwickeln, die den technischen Maßstab selbst setzen.

  • Hands-on bleiben: Rund 70 Prozent deiner Zeit verbringst du im Code, an den Problemen, bei denen dein Urteilsvermögen am meisten zählt. Der Rest entfällt auf technische und disziplinarische Führung.

  • Produktübergreifend Einfluss nehmen: Setze Architekturentscheidungen mit den Product Managern und Engineering Leads um, die die Roadmaps verantworten, die nicht in deinem Bereich liegen, und überzeuge dabei durch das bessere Argument statt durch Weisung.

  • Mit unserem Stack arbeiten: Python, pydantic-ai für Orchestrierung, Qdrant für Vektorsuche, Azure AI für Modelle, deployed auf Kubernetes in ein überwiegend JVM-basiertes (Kotlin, Micronaut) und Go-Backend.

Customer Success Manager

📍Manchester (Hybrid, up to 3 days WFH) | 💰 up to £33k (OTE up to £40k)


Street Group is one of the fastest-growing PropTech companies in the UK. We want to be the leading creator of delightful experiences for everybody involved in buying, selling, renting and letting property, regardless of their involvement, to improve the industry for everybody by elevating UK Estate Agencies through world-class technology.


As our client base rapidly expands, particularly among enterprise estate agencies, we are entering a pivotal moment of growth, so we’re investing in dedicated expertise to support our largest and most complex accounts. We want to drive the adoption of our products, and unlock long-term value through strategic partnerships. This is a key role in helping to shape the future of Enterprise customer success at Street Group.


Over the past six years, we've been working on Street.co.uk - our groundbreaking product that puts transparency, user experience, and beautiful design at the heart of the property industry. Joining our dynamic and ambitious Street.co.uk team, you will be a dedicated product specialist for our customers as they begin their journey with Street, driving client success while identifying opportunities for growth and long-term value across Street Group's ecosystem of products.


You will have the autonomy of planning your diary and workshops whilst making sure you are constantly going above and beyond for our customers in helping them find their way around the system, and the chance to make a genuine impact as we scale the business.


A bit about you…

  • You’ll have a background in Customer Success, ideally within the tech/SaaS space

  • You have excellent written and verbal communication skills (fluency in written and spoken English)

  • You're a dependable, motivated, self-starter, with the ability to work independently and the inner drive to grow a company that is in an exciting period of rapid growth

  • You're highly organised with exceptional attention to detail

title: Founding Product Builder, Operations
description:
Odin is building the investment infrastructure for the future of private markets.
We believe capital is one of the most powerful tools for shaping the world - and more people should know how to put it to work. Our mission is to make it radically easier to raise and deploy capital, so that anyone, anywhere, can back the companies and ideas they believe in.

Our first product is a full-stack platform for launching and running private investment firms, allowing you to run everything from your phone - think Shopify for VC and PE. We handle all the infrastructure: from legal structuring and investor onboarding to KYC/AML, payments, tax, reporting, and exits.

title: Web Developer (all genders)
description:
Your creative field

We are looking for a full-time, permanent Web Developer (all genders) to start as soon as possible. We live remote-first within Germany, but you have the freedom to choose whether you want to work hybrid or completely on-site due to your proximity to one of our locations.


What makes a good web developer? Not just that they code beautifully – but that they also know everything is still running at 3 a.m. Here, you work according to the "you build it, you run it" principle: full ownership, a modern tech stack, and AI-assisted development that lets you actively shape the architecture of our website.

That's exactly who we're looking for. Not a developer who hands off their code and then watches what happens to it, but someone who builds it, runs it, and stands behind it. For us, "you build it, you run it" isn't a saying that sounds nice – it's everyday reality:
 you write a feature, test it, push it live, and if something wobbles afterward, you're the one who sets it straight again. Not because no one else is around, but because you know best what you built. No blame game, no ticket disappearing into another team's queue, no "that's not my problem anymore" – real ownership, from the first commit to stable operation in production.

What does that look like in practice? On a typical day, you work on new features for our website, often supported by AI-assisted, agentic coding – not as a gimmick, but as a completely normal tool in your everyday work. You exchange ideas with the team, bring your own thinking to the architecture, and help make decisions rather than just implementing specs. You deploy through continuous delivery, keep an eye on how your code behaves in production, and when something isn't running smoothly, you dig into it yourself instead of waiting for someone else to.

You work with a modern stack (Astro, SvelteKit, TypeScript) and have the freedom to actively shape the architecture of our website – not as a bystander, but as someone whose fingerprints are visible in the end result. We're not interested in celebrating process for its own sake; what matters to us is that good ideas find their way into production quickly: short paths, a lot of trust, and little bureaucracy.


What convinces us

Your personality, paired with: 

  • 3–5 years of hands-on experience in web development (agency or in-house)
  • Strong, proven expertise with Astro, SvelteKit (SSG & SSR) and TypeScript

title: Platform & Reliability Engineer (all genders)
description:
Your creative field

We are looking for a full-time, permanent Platform & Reliability Engineer (all genders) to start as soon as possible. We live remote-first, but you have the freedom to choose whether you want to work hybrid or completely on-site due to your proximity to one of our locations (Berlin, Cologne, Hamburg, Munich).


As a Platform & Reliability Engineer at Contabo, you take architectural ownership of our shared infrastructure services – the foundation that multiple development teams build on: API gateway and ingress (Kong, Nginx Ingress), persistent storage (Ceph, Longhorn), secrets and identity infrastructure (Vault, Keycloak), edge security and WAF (Cloudflare), and our observability stack. You'll be taking over grown, partially under-documented systems – and that's exactly where the appeal of this role lies: you work your way deep into these systems, identify and remediate known weak points, evaluate aging components with solution-agnostic build-vs-buy reasoning, and decide which legacy pieces get fixed, replaced, or retired.

One of your central mandates: you design and establish an on-call process, including runbooks for platform and infrastructure incidents – where no formal process exists today. In parallel, you mature our observability practices, rolling out distributed tracing, SLOs/SLIs, and meaningful dashboards across the stack, building on our existing tooling with Prometheus, Grafana, Alloy, and OpenTelemetry. In system design reviews, you bring your strong grounding in the fundamentals – load balancing, caching, sharding, replication, consistency trade-offs – and apply them to new and existing services alike.

You won't be managing a team, but you will be the technical authority multiple teams rely on: you advise across teams on shared infrastructure services, document your knowledge consistently, and actively distribute it – so that critical know-how never again depends on a single person. Success in this role means: known risks are resolved, a solid on-call process is up and running, and single points of failure are measurably reduced platform-wide. The position is remote (Germany), with hybrid or on-site work optional; occasional travel for datacenter visits and team offsites is part of the role.


What convinces us

Your personality, paired with: 

  • 7+ years of experience in platform, infrastructure, or SRE roles, ideally with end-to-end responsibility for a private cloud or IaaS platform 
  • Hands-on production experience with distributed storage systems (Ceph) and Kubernetes persistent storage (Longhorn or comparable)

title: Strategic Account Director
description:
About Plentific

Plentific is redefining how property is managed in real time. Our cloud-based platform, supply chain and services help landlords run repairs, maintenance and compliance faster, with the data to make decisions instantly.

In the UK, we partner with housing associations and local authorities to tackle the sector's biggest challenges: repairs performance, disrepair, damp and mould, compliance and tenant satisfaction.

We're backed by world-class investors including Noa, Highland Europe, Brookfield, Mubadala, RXR Digital Ventures and Target Global. Headquartered in London with a global outlook, we're working towards managing over 2 million properties through our platform.

The Role

As Strategic Account Director, you'll own the full sales cycle across UK social housing, from sourcing your own pipeline to closing and growing multi-year partnerships with housing associations and local authorities.

You'll sell our SaaS platform alongside our transactional (TX) offerings, including Open Framework and Plentific Services. That means shaping blended deals that combine software, supply chain and delivery of works into one outcome for the client.

This is a hunter role with real ownership. You'll run your own discovery, demos and business cases, land new logos, expand existing accounts and own renewals. We'll back you with the tools, data and enablement to win.

You'll report into the Head of Sales. We're open to hybrid, London office-based or fully remote working.

What you'll do

Build your own pipeline

  • Self-generate the majority of your opportunities through outbound, sector networks, events and partners

  • Use our CRM, sales intelligence and AI tooling to research accounts, prioritise targets and run multi-channel outreach

  • Represent Plentific at sector conferences and exhibitions, and lead round-table discussions with housing leaders

Run the full sales cycle, end to end

  • Lead discovery and deliver tailored product demos yourself

  • Build ROI analyses and business cases with the toolkit we provide

  • Navigate public sector procurement: frameworks, direct awards and competitive tenders

  • Multi-thread across executive buying committees, including Directors of Property, Asset Management, Repairs, Finance and Procurement

  • Qualify rigorously, run mutual action plans and negotiate through to close

title: Forward Deployed AI Engineer
description:
Forward Deployed AI Engineer

Build end-to-end products on a solid data foundation, with AI as a force multiplier.

Data Practice | Remote (Poland) | Senior

 

About TechTorch

At TechTorch, we’re building the future of intelligent work. Our mission is to help companies design, build, and deploy AI agents that automate complex, real-world workflows — delivering reliability, measurable ROI, and massive efficiency gains.

Here, you won’t just be playing with prompts or running endless proofs of concept. You’ll ship production-grade AI systems that solve real problems across industries.

You’ll join a hands-on, fast-moving, ownership-driven team that thrives on building quickly, iterating fast, and seeing results in days — not months.

 

About the Practice

TechTorch's Data Practice sits at the intersection of enterprise data and applied AI. We design and build AI-native systems that don't just analyze the past — they actively drive decisions. Our work spans data infrastructure and pipelines, intelligent automation, and full-stack AI applications across industries.

We work the way the best client-delivery teams now operate: small teams, deep ownership, no hand-offs at boundaries. We take problems from a client whiteboard to production, and we let AI do the heavy lifting wherever it earns its place.

The Role

We're looking for an engineer who builds across the full stack and owns the data underneath it. You can sit in a client session, shape the architecture, design the data foundation, and ship the application that runs on top of it — without handing off at the boundaries.

The work spans client delivery and internal accelerator development. You map the problem, structure the solution, and own the outcome from end to end. AI coding agents are central to how we build — not a novelty, but the daily layer that lets a small team cover a lot of ground.

What You'll Do

  • Own work end to end — from discovery and solution shaping through system design, build, and production deployment.

  • Design and build the data foundation: data models, schema design, dimensional modeling, ETL/ELT pipelines, and slowly changing dimensions (SCD)

title: Enterprise Sales Lead - Healthcare
description:
About ElevenLabs

ElevenLabs is an AI research and product company transforming how we interact with technology.

We launched in January 2023 with the first human-like AI voice model. Today, we serve millions of users and thousands of businesses - from fast-growing startups to large enterprises like Deutsche Telekom and Meta. Our investors are some of the world's most prominent, including Andreessen Horowitz, ICONIQ Growth and Sequoia. We've raised $781M in funding and our last valuation was $22B - multiples of 11, always.

We have expanded from voice into three main platforms:

  • ElevenAgents enables businesses to deliver seamless and intelligent customer experiences, with the integrations, testing, monitoring, and reliability necessary to deploy voice and chat agents at scale.

  • ElevenCreative empowers creators and marketers to generate and edit speech, music, image, and video across 70+ languages.

  • ElevenAPI gives developers access to our leading AI audio foundational models.

Everything we do is the result of the creativity and commitment of our team - builders doing the best work of their lives. We are researchers, engineers, and operators. IOI medalists and ex-founders. If you want to work hard and create lasting positive impact, we want to hear from you.

How we work

  • High-velocity: Rapid experimentation, lean autonomous teams, and minimal bureaucracy.

  • Impact not job titles: We don’t have job titles. Instead, it’s about the impact you have. No task is above or beneath you.

  • AI first: We use AI to move faster with higher-quality results. We do this across the whole company—from engineering to growth to operations.

  • Excellence everywhere: Everything we do should match the quality of our AI models.

  • Global team: We prioritize your talent, not your location.

What we offer

  • Innovative culture: You’ll be part of a generational opportunity to define the trajectory of AI, surrounded by a team pushing the boundaries of what’s possible.

  • Growth paths: Joining ElevenLabs means joining a dynamic team with countless opportunities to drive impact - beyond your immediate role and responsibilities.

  • Learning & development: Eleve

title: Security Engineer (Hybrid or Remote)
description:
About The Role

We’re looking for a Security Engineer to own and improve the security of our internal environment — the identities, SaaS apps, endpoints, AI tooling, and networks our employees use every day. This is a hands-on senior role: we expect you to design controls, find the gaps, and drive the changes that close them — and to build the automation that makes it scale.

We’re an EMI-licensed fintech in a fully cloud-native AWS environment, we use AI heavily, and we’re growing fast. We need someone who can lead technical initiatives independently, influence our security architecture, challenge approaches that no longer fit, and explain it clearly to engineers and leadership.


Your Mission

Detection & Response (SIEM) — our top priority

  • Own SIEM alerting end-to-end: ship logs from endpoints, IdP, VPN, SaaS, and cloud; write and tune detection rules; cut false positives.
  • Act as first responder for security incidents — investigate, contain, drive to closure with clear runbooks — and feed recurring issues back into preventive controls.
Identity, Access & SaaS
  • Administer the IdP (SSO via SAML/OIDC, MFA, conditional access) and run access recertification end-to-end across IdP, SaaS, AWS, and internal tools — scope, evidence, follow-through on revocations.
  • Hunt down over-permissive and stale access, enforce least privilege and PAM, catch SoD gaps, and make JML and third-party access work in practice.
  • Improve SaaS security posture (Google/Microsoft, Slack, GitHub, others) and apply DLP controls to limit data leakage.
Endpoint, Email & Phishing Defense
  • Keep the endpoint stack healthy and well-tuned — MDM, XDR/AV, device-compliance checks for VPN/ZTNA — and define posture requirements (disk encryption, EDR present, OS version) with automated remediation.
  • Defend against phishing and spoofing — secure email gateway rules, DMARC/SPF/DKIM — and run phishing simulations and security awareness, acting on the results.
Automation & Ownership
  • Build internal tooling and automate repetitive operations — reduce manual work, don't just operate it.
  • Own the roadmap for your areas: identify gaps, lead initiatives independently, and raise the bar rather than just maintain it.


Your Profile

  • 5+ years in security operations, corporate/IT security, or endpoint engineering.
  • Strong with a SIEM (Splunk, Elastic, Panther, Sumo Logic) — detection engineering and incident response — plus an identity provider (Okta, Entra ID, Google Workspace), access recertification, and least-privilege / PAM.
  • Working knowledge of endpoint security (MDM, XDR/EDR/AV) and email / phishing defense.
  • Practical experience securing how a company uses AI internally: shadow AI discovery,

  • Develop efficient systems for large-scale multimodal datasets, including imagery, LiDAR, odometry, ground truth, and simulation data.

  • Establish dataset and model versioning, metadata management, quality checks, and traceability from raw sensor data to validated model artifacts.

  • Build and optimize distributed training workflows, job scheduling, GPU resource allocation, caching, and high-throughput data access.

title: Engineering Team Lead, Serverless Containers
description:
About Mistral

Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms.

We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited.

The team

Mistral is building a sovereign AI cloud for Europe. Our customers in finance, healthcare, and the public sector run frontier models on European-jurisdiction infrastructure, and the Cloud Platform team builds the systems that make that possible — compute orchestration, Kubernetes, bare metal, storage, networking, and the datacenter fleet that runs it all.

We run it all on our own metal, our own network, our own datacenters — which means when something breaks, the fix is ours to write.

European Compute Units let enterprises commit to multi-year capacity on that infrastructure, and we are scaling toward a gigawatt of compute across Europe by 2030. You will design and ship the layer every sovereign AI deployment depends on and shape the team building it.

The Role

This is a people-leadership role from day one. You will manage the team — hiring, coaching, performance, growth paths, honest feedback — while staying close to the code: roughly half your time in architecture decisions and the hardest technical problems the team faces, the other half leading your squad. If you are looking for a senior IC role, this is not it.

You will lead the team building our serverless containers product: the way developers run AI apps, MCP servers, APIs, and managed workers on our cloud without thinking about servers. Push a container, get an endpoint, scale from zero to thousands of instances and back down — across CPU and GPU.

On a hyperscaler, the serverless layer is a product someone else built. Here you own it end to end: the scheduler that decides where a container lands, the routing path a request takes, the machinery that turns a scaled-to-zero service into a warm instance before a customer notices. All of it runs on metal, network, and datacenters we own.

title: SRE / Platform Engineer (all genders) - Remote Germany
description:
About Linro

Linro is a Berlin-based cloud security company building a real-time, agentic cloud-security platform. Teams ship with AI. AI ships with Linro.

Infrastructure changes constantly, and increasingly it's AI agents making the changes. Tools that scan snapshots and flag risk after the fact can't keep up. Linro enforces intended state across the whole lifecycle instead, from commit to runtime: MCP and pre-commit hooks at commit time, blast-radius simulation that blocks bad changes before they ship, and real-time detection, enforcement and auto-remediation in production. Most tools tell you what's wrong. Linro stops it.

We have each been on the receiving end of this problem: Running cloud security at scale, building the platforms underneath it, and shipping in regulated systems where a wrong change isn't an option. Founded in Berlin in 2026 and built fully remote across Europe, Linro has a platform that's real and working, with plenty still to shape.

The role

You would be one of our first infrastructure hires, taking day-to-day operation of the platform off the CTO. Linro enforces policy on other people's cloud infrastructure, so our own has to be reliable, reproducible and auditable. You own production: how Linro runs for each customer, how it upgrades, and how we know it is unhealthy before a customer does.

What you will do

  • Own production reliability: SLOs, alerting, on-call and blameless postmortems for the control plane and every customer installation.

  • Make the install fleet boring: provisioning, maintenance windows and safe auto-upgrades across SaaS and self-hosted installs.

  • Fix the open reliability work: sensor memory ceilings and OOM visibility, ClickHouse cost and capacity, and the health of Postgres, PGMQ and Temporal.

  • Evolve the platform: Terraform and Terragrunt, Helm, GitHub Actions with short-lived OIDC credentials, local development (Tilt, Coder), and staging and production environments, with guardrails for humans and AI agents alike.

  • Produce audit-ready operations: backups, disaster recovery and continuity tests with evidence for SOC 2 and ISO 27001.

What we are looking for

  • Hands-on operation of AWS, GCP or Azure in production, AWS preferred. Not just deploying to it, actually running it: accounts and access management, networking and the failure modes. We run across several clouds, so you pick up the others quickly.

  • 3+

title: Infrastructure Engineer (ML Systems) - Paris
description:
You’ll own the GPU compute that powers our model training, evaluation and serving systems.

This role sits in our Infrastructure team, which works at the lowest layers of our stack, from Kubernetes down to the GPU hardware. You’ll run the clusters, GPUs and schedulers that our research, product and platform teams depend on, and manage the capacity we buy from our cloud providers.

What success looks like

Success is measured by how well we use our GPUs: keeping production reliable and improving the performance of our training and serving stack.

What you’ll be doing

  • Running Kubernetes clusters for GPU training and inference

  • Improving how GPU work is scheduled and placed

  • Detecting, draining and repairing unhealthy GPU nodes

  • Managing capacity with our cloud providers

  • Debugging failures in GPUs, Linux, storage and networking

The first year

By month 3, you’ll be handling a share of cluster incidents on your own and will have shipped one change to scheduling or node health, such as automatically detecting and draining unhealthy GPU nodes. By month 6, you’ll own one part of the compute layer outright: scheduling and placement, node health and repair, or capacity and new regions. By month 12, you’ll be responsible for a globally distributed GPU system that shifts capacity between training and inference as needs change.

Who you’ll work with

Your hiring manager is our VP of Engineering. Day to day, you’ll work with the Platform Infrastructure team, the research and product teams who use our compute, and our cloud providers and other vendors.

What we think it takes

You’re likely a good fit if you:

  • Have built and run GPU workloads on Kubernetes

  • Could design a GPU cluster for training and online RL from scratch

  • Debug confidently at the OS layer and below (Linux, GPU drivers, networking and storage)

  • Write strong Python

It’s a plus if you’ve worked as an SRE or infrastructure engineer, or have used:

  • Slurm

  • Kubernetes scheduling and autoscaling tools such as Kueue or Karpenter

title: Senior Backend Engineer (Java) — IoT Remote Monitoring & Energy Management System

title: Security Engineer (Hybrid or Remote)
description:
About The Role

We’re looking for a Security Engineer to own and improve the security of our internal environment — the identities, SaaS apps, endpoints, AI tooling, and networks our employees use every day. This is a hands-on senior role: we expect you to design controls, find the gaps, and drive the changes that close them — and to build the automation that makes it scale.

We’re an EMI-licensed fintech in a fully cloud-native AWS environment, we use AI heavily, and we’re growing fast. We need someone who can lead technical initiatives independently, influence our security architecture, challenge approaches that no longer fit, and explain it clearly to engineers and leadership.


Your Mission

title: Web Developer (all genders)
description:
Your creative field

We are looking for a full-time, permanent Web Developer (all genders) to start as soon as possible. We live remote-first within Germany, but you have the freedom to choose whether you want to work hybrid or completely on-site due to your proximity to one of our locations.


What makes a good web developer? Not just that they code beautifully – but that they also know everything is still running at 3 a.m. Here, you work according to the "you build it, you run it" principle: full ownership, a modern tech stack, and AI-assisted development that lets you actively shape the architecture of our website.

That's exactly who we're looking for. Not a developer who hands off their code and then watches what happens to it, but someone who builds it, runs it, and stands behind it. For us, "you build it, you run it" isn't a saying that sounds nice – it's everyday reality:
 you write a feature, test it, push it live, and if something wobbles afterward, you're the one who sets it straight again. Not because no one else is around, but because you know best what you built. No blame game, no ticket disappearing into another team's queue, no "that's not my problem anymore" – real ownership, from the first commit to stable operation in production.

What does that look like in practice? On a typical day, you work on new features for our website, often supported by AI-assisted, agentic coding – not as a gimmick, but as a completely normal tool in your everyday work. You exchange ideas with the team, bring your own thinking to the architecture, and help make decisions rather than just implementing specs. You deploy through continuous delivery, keep an eye on how your code behaves in production, and when something isn't running smoothly, you dig into it yourself instead of waiting for someone else to.

You work with a modern stack (Astro, SvelteKit, TypeScript) and have the freedom to actively shape the architecture of our website – not as a bystander, but as someone whose fingerprints are visible in the end result. We're not interested in celebrating process for its own sake; what matters to us is that good ideas find their way into production quickly: short paths, a lot of trust, and little bureaucracy.


What convinces us

Your personality, paired with: 

  • 3–5 years of hands-on experience in web development (agency or in-house)
  • Strong, proven expertise with Astro, SvelteKit (SSG & SSR) and TypeScript

title: Platform & Reliability Engineer (all genders)
description:
Your creative field

We are looking for a full-time, permanent Platform & Reliability Engineer (all genders) to start as soon as possible. We live remote-first, but you have the freedom to choose whether you want to work hybrid or completely on-site due to your proximity to one of our locations (Berlin, Cologne, Hamburg, Munich).


As a Platform & Reliability Engineer at Contabo, you take architectural ownership of our shared infrastructure services – the foundation that multiple development teams build on: API gateway and ingress (Kong, Nginx Ingress), persistent storage (Ceph, Longhorn), secrets and identity infrastructure (Vault, Keycloak), edge security and WAF (Cloudflare), and our observability stack. You'll be taking over grown, partially under-documented systems – and that's exactly where the appeal of this role lies: you work your way deep into these systems, identify and remediate known weak points, evaluate aging components with solution-agnostic build-vs-buy reasoning, and decide which legacy pieces get fixed, replaced, or retired.

One of your central mandates: you design and establish an on-call process, including runbooks for platform and infrastructure incidents – where no formal process exists today. In parallel, you mature our observability practices, rolling out distributed tracing, SLOs/SLIs, and meaningful dashboards across the stack, building on our existing tooling with Prometheus, Grafana, Alloy, and OpenTelemetry. In system design reviews, you bring your strong grounding in the fundamentals – load balancing, caching, sharding, replication, consistency trade-offs – and apply them to new and existing services alike.

You won't be managing a team, but you will be the technical authority multiple teams rely on: you advise across teams on shared infrastructure services, document your knowledge consistently, and actively distribute it – so that critical know-how never again depends on a single person. Success in this role means: known risks are resolved, a solid on-call process is up and running, and single points of failure are measurably reduced platform-wide. The position is remote (Germany), with hybrid or on-site work optional; occasional travel for datacenter visits and team offsites is part of the role.


What convinces us

Your personality, paired with: 

  • 7+ years of experience in platform, infrastructure, or SRE roles, ideally with end-to-end responsibility for a private cloud or IaaS platform 
  • Hands-on production experience with distributed storage systems (Ceph) and Kubernetes persistent storage (Longhorn or comparable)

As a Senior Embedded Software Test Engineer at Optics11, you own the embedded software system-test capability for our sensing interrogator platforms. Your scope covers the integrated behavior of embedded Linux applications and services, internal and external APIs, hardware interfaces, firmware and FPGA interactions, system control, calibration and configuration, diagnostics, data acquisition, boot and update behavior, recovery mechanisms, and sensor interfaces. You build and maintain automated test frameworks, HIL benches, test harnesses, CI/CD integration, and objective release evidence that make product behavior repeatable, observable, and measurable.

You are part of the Sensing Platform Team and work closely with Embedded Software, FPGA/Firmware, Electronics, Photonics, Architects, Product System Engineering, Product Integration, Verification & Validation, Lifecycle Engineering, application/software teams, and external development partners. The primary ownership of this role is integrated interrogator/HIL system-level testing and release qualification. It complements developer-owned unit and component testing and does not replace independent formal verification, compliance, environmental, or end-to-end application validation performed downstream.

title: Client Partner
description:
Odin is building the investment infrastructure for the future of private markets.
We believe capital is one of the most powerful tools for shaping the world - and more people should know how to put it to work. Our mission is to make it radically easier to raise and deploy capital, so that anyone, anywhere, can back the companies and ideas they believe in.

Our first product is a full-stack platform for launching and running private investment firms, allowing you to run everything from your phone - think Shopify for VC and PE. We handle all the infrastructure: from legal structuring and investor onboarding to KYC/AML, payments, tax, reporting, and exits.

We're already trusted by over 10,000 angels, VCs, and founders. We administer over $750m in assets, covering investments from pre-seed to series E. This includes household names like ElevenLabs, OpenAI, SpaceX, xAI, Anduril, etc. but also new companies creating everything from synthetic brains to small nuclear reactors.

Why we're hiring

  • We're on track for roughly 700 deals a year and $750m in investment flowing through Odin in 2026. The goal is 7,000 deals a year.

  • Inbound is already around 70 new leads a month and climbing. You won't be cold calling. The demand is here, and your job is to turn it into deals.

  • Our customers are angels, syndicate leads and fund managers backing the most interesting companies in the world. When they're doing a deal, you're the person they call.

  • Every customer you bring in becomes part of your book, and your commission grows with it.

  • You'll be one of the first people in our commercial team, shaping how we sell as we scale from here.

What you'll own

  • Converting inbound: A steady flow of inbound lands with you every week. You decide quickly which leads have a real deal behind them and turn them into their first deal on Odin, spending your time where it pays off.

Ops, compliance and legal do the work; you run the deal, know exactly what's closing this week and what's in the way, and make it happen. That's the trust that brings customers back.

title: SEO Manager (m/f/d)
description:
About the Job

We're looking for an SEO Manager to get hands-on with our affiliate portfolio and grow it. You'll work directly with some of the biggest publishers in the world, and your work will show up in the numbers — fast.

You'll work across two areas: driving more revenue out of affiliate sites that are already live, and helping take brand-new sites from a blank page to go-live — keyword clustering, content structure, stakeholder coordination, the whole build. Every Google update, every new market, every publisher conversation is something you'll get your hands on.

At WLX, SEO isn't a support function — it's a driving force. We have the resources, the management backing, and the hands-on expertise to make things happen. And unlike an agency, everything we build is ours: our own projects, run in close collaboration with the world's biggest publishers. That means real ownership, real impact, and no client briefs.

This is what you'll do

  • Drive revenue growth on existing affiliate sites: Develop and implement long-term SEO strategies, and own the on-page and off-page work that moves the needle.
  • Improve and maintain rankings on key money pages: Run content audits, apply intent mapping, and improve CTR and SERP feature capture on your highest-value pages.
  • Lead backlink campaigns: Build and execute link-building strategies across multiple affiliate sites, working with agencies, forums, and outreach partners to strengthen domain authority.
  • Help take new affiliate sites live: Own keyword clustering, topic mapping, and content structure based on market and competitor research, and coordinate with stakeholders to get new sites launched from scratch.
  • React fast when the landscape shifts: Assess the impact of Google algorithm updates, figure out what happened and why, and put a clear plan in place to recover traffic — without getting stuck in the noise.

This is what you’ve got

  • Extensive SEO experience, with strong, hands-on expertise in both on-page and off-page work, and a track record of driving organic growth at scale.
  • Fluent in German and English, confident in operating with stakeholders in both languages.
  • Strong analytical thinking and prioritisation skills — you know what moves the needle and can back your decisions with data.
  • Proactive and self-motivated, comfortable owning your workstream without needing to be told what's next.
  • Comfortable working in a fast-paced, flat, startup-style environment.
  • Experience in iGaming or other affiliate marketing industries is a plus.

We are hiring on behalf of our client, a fast-growing innovator in the crypto and decentralized finance space who is seeking a Founding Platform Engineer (Staff+ level) to join the team. This organization is behind a leading decentralized exchange (DEX) on HyperEVM, having achieved significant revenue milestones with an ultra-lean team. The client is now expanding its technical architecture to build an advanced, mobile-first crypto trading platform (spot + perps) alongside a novel, original social product featuring cutting-edge mechanisms.

title: Founding Platform Engineer
description:
We are hiring on behalf of our client, a fast-growing innovator in the crypto and decentralized finance space who is seeking a Founding Platform Engineer (Staff+ level) to join the team. This organization is behind a leading decentralized exchange (DEX) on HyperEVM, having achieved significant revenue milestones with an ultra-lean team. The client is now expanding its technical architecture to build an advanced, mobile-first crypto trading platform (spot + perps) alongside a novel, original social product featuring cutting-edge mechanisms.

As the first and only engineer in this specialized domain, the incoming candidate will take an original product vision and turn it into a robust, high-performance system—holding the entire architecture and the smallest details simultaneously. The operational environment is primarily asynchronous, highly independent, and built for top-tier developers who can scale infrastructure from zero to massive daily trading volumes while maintaining absolute reliability.

Requirements

  • Platform Ownership: Own the core platform, including the data layer, rewards engine, notifications, the API surface, and overall system reliability.
  • Trading Engine Integration: Integrate perpetual trading engines through Hyperliquid, alongside spot trading via Jupiter and Relay.
  • Data Harmonization: Aggregate and unify conflicting data providers (such as Zerion, CoinGecko, Mobula, Alchemy, and Hyperliquid) into a single, cohesive source of truth.
  • High-Performance Data Delivery: Serve heavy data rapidly by implementing resilient caching mechanisms that survive traffic stampedes and fan-out structures that hold under pressure.
  • Cross-Chain Abstraction: Design architecture that makes a single USDC balance across multiple chains entirely invisible and seamless to the end user.
  • Peak Performance & Reliability: Maintain absolute uptime during peak market volatility; ensure the application never lags or crashes when it matters most, guaranteeing users can always close positions.

﻿

Requirements

  • Proven track record of engineering resilience, including keeping a high-stakes system alive through massive traffic spikes and determining graceful degradation strategies in advance.
  • Extensive experience building financial rewards and accounting systems that withstand retries, prioritizing idempotency, replay safety, and precise lot tracking.
  • Deep understanding of end-to-end latency budgets (from a user's tap to screen rendering).
  • Advanced database optimization skills, capable of resolving bottlenecks directly within PostgreSQL rather than relying on secondary databases.
  • Strong proficiency in Rust development.
  • Comfortable working in a fast-paced, remote environment across North American or Euro

description:
Consequential Work. Dedicated People.


About Onebrief

Onebrief builds collaboration and AI-powered workflow software for military planning and operational coordination.

Military planning is complex by nature, requiring teams to coordinate information, people, and decisions across systems and locations. Onebrief brings planning, collaboration, simulation, and AI into one connected environment, helping teams test strategies, adapt to changing conditions, and make decisions with greater clarity when the stakes are real.

We are a distributed team of builders from military, operational, and technology backgrounds who care deeply about improving how important work gets done. Some team members work remotely, while others work directly alongside customers in operational environments around the world.

Founded in 2019, Onebrief is backed by leading investors including General Catalyst, Battery Ventures, Insight Partners, Sapphire Ventures, and Human Capital. Valued at more than $2 billion, we continue to invest in product innovation, AI capabilities, and team growth.

We are hiring a Site Reliability Engineer to support Onebrief deployments across on-premises hardware, virtualized systems, and cloud environments.

This is a hands-on infrastructure role focused on Linux administration, hardware maintenance, and application reliability. title: Principal Software Engineer
description:
About Doit

We are focused on reinventing how people spend, save, invest, exchange, travel, and more. Our objective is to build tools that will help people get more from their money and become an expert at ease. We believe AI will help make finance smart, assessible and safe.

 

We are looking for the most talented and driven people we can find. We are looking for people who work for their passion, not counting hours. Who loves building great next-generation products, not status quo. Who cares about redefining how everyone around us can get the best financial applications, not for an exclusive few. We have teams working around the world, with over 20 nationalities and growing from our offices and remotely. Join us and build a better future for our society.

 

In 2019, we built the first mobile-first, insurance platform, enabling insurance to be accessible online by millions in the region. Today, it's the leading insurance platform in Southeast Asia.

The Role

Doit builds technology products used by millions of users across Southeast Asia. As our products and systems scale, we need technical leaders who can solve difficult engineering problems and raise the engineering bar around them.

The Principal Software Engineer owns technical direction and execution for major products and systems. This is a hands-on role - you will design systems, write code, and drive critical engineering work from idea to production.

 

What You'll Own

  • Owning technical design and execution for major products, systems and engineering initiatives.

  • Designing scalable, reliable systems across backend, frontend, APIs, databases and infrastructure.

  • Building alongside the team through coding, prototyping, code reviews, debugging and production problem-solving.

  • Driving architecture decisions and trade-offs across speed, scalability, reliability, cost and maintainability.

  • Turning ambiguous product problems into clear technical solutions and execution plans.

  • Raising engineering quality through stronger system design, testing, security, observability and development practices.

  • Leading technically critical initiatives and mentoring engineers across teams.

title: Software Engineer, Applied AI
description:
About CircuitHub

CircuitHub is reshaping electronics manufacturing with The Grid, a factory-scale robotics platform that makes small-batch, high-mix electronics assembly radically more efficient. Think semiconductor-fab precision applied to the chaotic world of prototyping and low-volume production: a 10x throughput improvement in one of the world's most foundational industries.

We've raised $45M from top-tier investors including Plural, Y Combinator and Google Ventures, and we're already profitable. Our customers include a major EV maker, a top AI lab and many of the worlds largest companies.

The Grid isn't a prototype. It's live, scaling fast and delivering real revenue, and we're building the team that will scale it further.

The Role

CircuitHub makes electronics on demand. Engineers upload a circuit board design; we buy the parts, build the board in our own robotic factory and ship it. More and more of that business is now run by AI agents, and we want you to help build them.

These aren't chatbots. Our agents have real jobs:

  • They inspect boards. An agent checks camera images of every panel we build for wrong, rotated or missing parts.

  • They program robots. Agents read datasheets so our pick-and-place machines know how to handle each new part.

  • They watch the factory. They spot stray parts in robot storage, diagnose printer faults and clear stuck machines.

  • They run the back office. They book supplier invoices, chase late orders, explain quotes and triage bugs.

  • They write our code. Most of what our team ships starts in an agent session.

What you'll do

Find a process people still do by hand and automate it end to end: decide what needs judgement and what needs plain code, build the tools, and prove it works before it runs alone. Then make it cheaper, faster and right more often. You'll also improve the platform every agent runs on, and work closely with the people your work serves, from factory operators to finance.

How we build

  • Evals first. An agent earns the right to work alone: blind tests against people's verdicts, shadow runs beside the humans, replays of past decisions. We track accuracy and cost per run, and re-test whenever we change a model, a prompt or the effort level.

  • Agents judge, code writes. Agents return structured answers. Plain code checks them against a second source and

Sparta is the AI leader for commodity trading, home to Leonidas AI, the first operating system for oil and commodity traders.

Backed by $42 million in Series B funding led by One Peak, with participation from returning investors FirstMark and Singular, the same investors behind AI leaders like Legora, Dataiku, and Synthesia. Most companies are building a chatbot on top of data. We've built an agent with an actual reasoning layer, grounded in years of proprietary market data and in-house trading expertise nobody else has.

We're scaling fast, and it's an exciting time to join. From independents to multinationals, the world's leading commodity teams use Sparta and Leonidas AI to move faster, trade smarter, and stay ahead of the market.

You'll be challenged, supported, and given room to grow, building the AI that's changing how commodity trading gets done.

Your work has reach. From shaping Leonidas AI, to powering smarter decisions for traders around the world, to changing how commodity trading is done. And because we're growing fast, you'll accelerate your career with a level of ownership and impact you simply won't get at bigger, slower-moving companies.

You’ll be handed context, and trusted to work out the right thing to build.

title: Community Manager
description:
Adaptyv is building an automated lab that lets AI agents run biology experiments.

We're entering the era of agentic science where AI models can now design novel proteins, propose hypotheses, and iterate on experimental results. But they can't run the experiments themselves - that's still a manual, months-long process. We're building the infrastructure that gives AI agents access to the physical world.

We are one of the fastest growing biotech companies, trusted by leading biopharmas, frontier AI labs, and the techbio companies pushing the field forward. This is a rare chance to help advance some of the most important work happening in biotech today.

Our automated lab is powered by a deep software + hardware stack: lab instruments worth millions of USD reverse-engineered into API-controllable hardware, dozens of devices orchestrated through complex workflows, full observability on everything that happens in the lab, processing pipelines for messy physical-world data, and AI systems that troubleshoot production results and accelerate assay development.

We’re growing rapidly and are hiring for talented people to scale and support the massive demand for AI-driven wet lab experimentation.

About the role

You'll be the person who makes sure Adaptyv shows up well in public, every day. That means managing our social presence across X and LinkedIn, running the Proteinbase community, owning the participant side of our open competitions and hackathons, and triaging inbound community and customer messages. Whatever it takes to keep our community-facing surface area healthy as we grow.

This is a hands-on, high-ownership role. You'll be the go-to person for anything community: content, social, events, and the day-to-day rhythm of how Adaptyv talks to the outside world. You'll work closely with the founders and the science team, and you'll have a direct impact on how the protein design and AI bio communities experience us.

description:
About Mistral

Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms.

We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited.

THE TEAM

Mistral is building a sovereign AI cloud for Europe. Our customers in finance, healthcare, and the public sector run frontier models on European-jurisdiction infrastructure, and the Cloud Platform team builds the systems that make that possible — compute orchestration, Kubernetes, bare metal, storage, networking, and the datacenter fleet that runs it all.

We run it all on our own metal, our own network, our own datacenters — which means when something breaks, the fix is ours to write.

European Compute Units let enterprises commit to multi-year capacity on that infrastructure, and we are scaling toward a gigawatt of compute across Europe by 2030. You will design and ship the layer every sovereign AI deployment depends on.

THE ROLE

You will build our Kubernetes product end to end: a metal-to-on-demand platform built on in-house infrastructure, with GPU support for training, inference, and general-purpose compute.

Kubernetes is our product, not just our platform — we run it on infrastructure we own end to end. You will decide how the control plane scales, how GPUs get scheduled, and how quickly a rack of bare metal becomes an on-demand cluster a customer can use. The decisions you make here shape how our infrastructure scales from today's footprint to a gigawatt, and how we turn frontier AI research into production systems used by millions.

WHAT YOU WILL DO

- Design and ship the control plane. You own the architecture and the hardest implementation decisions — scheduling, operators, provisioning, node lifecycle.

- Own the reliability of the Kubernetes control plane. It is the team's headline KPI. You make the calls when it breaks at 3am.

- Shrink the distance from metal to on-demand. Provisioning a cluster should be minutes of automation, not weeks of tickets.

European Compute Units let enterprises commit to multi-year capacity on that infrastructure, and we are scaling toward a gigawatt of compute across Europe by 2030. You will design and ship the layer every sovereign AI deployment depends on.

THE ROLE

AI agents don't run in browsers. They run in sandboxes — and you will build ours.

We build secure, isolated, network-controlled environments with snapshotting primitives, designed for AI agents and reinforcement-learning workloads. An RL training run doesn't need one environment; it needs thousands, created and destroyed every second. An agent needs to be sandboxed from the world while still feeling fast enough to be useful. That tension — airtight isolation, at fleet scale, at low latency — is the product.

Your customers are the people building the next generation of AI software on our infrastructure; the primitives you ship become the runtime their agents live in.

WHAT YOU WILL DO

- Build the isolation layer: microVMs or containers, namespaces, cgroups, seccomp, snapshot and restore.

- Own the security boundary. Customers run code they didn't write and can't fully trust — your systems make that safe.

- Scale to fleets: creation latency, density, and lifecycle management for thousands of concurrent environments.
